_about: Starter Codex glossary for the EMC app. DRAFT. D&D meanings follow the 2024 rules (SRD 5.2). Status: ready = plain meaning is general knowledge or taken from the live app; confirm = general meaning is given but the EMC version needs John's OK; john_to_fill = EMC-specific, nothing written on purpose.

terms.plain: How much harm you can take before you drop.
terms.inTheGame: At 0 HP you fall unconscious. Rest and healing bring HP back.

terms.plain: How hard you are to hit. An attack has to roll at least your AC to land.
terms.inTheGame: With no armor, AC is 10 plus your Dexterity modifier.

terms.plain: Who acts first when a fight starts.
terms.inTheGame: Everyone rolls a d20 and adds their Dexterity modifier. Highest goes first.

terms.plain: How far you can move on your turn, in feet.
terms.inTheGame: 30 feet is typical for a starting character.

terms.plain: The six traits that describe your character: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma.
terms.inTheGame: Each one has a score. The score gives you a modifier you add to rolls.
terms.inRealLife: In the Company, your real life builds them: workouts, nutrition and sleep, mental goals and social goals.

terms.plain: Raw power: lifting, pushing, carrying.
terms.inTheGame: Your Strength modifier helps with Athletics and with lifting, pushing or breaking things.

terms.plain: Balance, speed and quick reflexes.
terms.inTheGame: Your Dexterity modifier adds to Initiative, to AC while lightly armored, and to Acrobatics, Sleight of Hand and Stealth.

terms.plain: How tough you are: your stamina, and how well you shake off hits.
terms.inTheGame: Your Constitution modifier adds to your hit points every time you level up.

terms.plain: Memory and clear thinking.
terms.inTheGame: Your Intelligence modifier helps with knowledge skills like History.

terms.plain: Awareness and good judgment.
terms.inTheGame: Your Wisdom modifier helps with skills like Insight, Perception and Animal Handling.

terms.plain: How well you connect with people.
terms.inTheGame: Your Charisma modifier helps with Deception, Persuasion, Intimidation and Performance.

terms.plain: The number you add to a die roll. It comes from an ability score.
terms.inTheGame: A score of 10 or 11 gives +0. Every 2 points up or down moves it by 1. A score of 9 gives -1.

terms.plain: Being trained at something. You add your proficiency bonus when you roll for it.
terms.inTheGame: The bonus is +2 at level 1 and grows as you level up. Your background decides some of your trained skills.

terms.plain: A specific thing you can be good at, like Athletics or Insight. Each skill belongs to one ability.
terms.inTheGame: To use a skill you roll a d20 and add the ability modifier, plus your proficiency bonus if you are trained.

terms.plain: A roll to see whether you succeed at something uncertain.
terms.inTheGame: Roll a d20 and add a modifier. Meet or beat the target number (the DC) and you succeed.

terms.plain: The number you need to meet or beat on a roll.
terms.inTheGame: The DM sets it. Easy things have a low DC and hard things a high one.

terms.plain: A roll to resist harm or a sudden effect.
terms.inTheGame: Roll a d20 and add the matching ability modifier, plus your proficiency bonus if you are trained in that save.

terms.plain: Roll two d20s and keep the higher one.
terms.inTheGame: If something helps you, you get advantage. If you have both advantage and disadvantage, they cancel out.

terms.plain: Roll two d20s and keep the lower one.
terms.inTheGame: If something hinders you, you get disadvantage.

terms.plain: A twenty-sided die. Most important rolls in D&D use it.
terms.inTheGame: Roll it, add your modifier, and compare the total to a target number.

terms.plain: Shorthand for a roll. 2d6+3 means roll two six-sided dice, add them up, then add 3.
terms.inTheGame: The first number is how many dice. The number after the d is how many sides.

terms.plain: The person who runs the game. They describe the world, play the other characters and settle the rules.
How far along your character is. Higher levels unlock more.
terms.inTheGame: You start at level 1. Levels raise your hit points and your proficiency bonus.
terms.emcNote: [John to fill: what earns a level at EMC, and what the progress ring should measure]

terms.plain: Your character's profession, like Fighter or Rogue. It decides what you are best at.
What kind of being your character is, such as human, dwarf or elf. Older books call this race.
Where your character came from before the Company. In the 2024 rules it also gives you skills, a tool and a starting talent.
terms.inTheGame: Pick a background and the app fills in the matching skills and tools for you.

terms.plain: A small talent. In the 2024 rules your background gives you one to start.
The Empire Mercenary Company: the group you are joining. You train, keep each other accountable and play the story together.
Your team inside the Company. You train, check in and play the story alongside them.
terms.emcNote: [John to fill: how squads are assigned and how big they are]

terms.plain: One sitting of play, usually a few hours.
terms.inTheGame: In D&D, one session is one stretch of the story.
terms.emcNote: [John to fill: what a session is at EMC and how players pick a time. The app shows slots 9-12, 2-5 and 7-10 (18+).]

terms.plain: Your weekly report. Four quick questions about workouts and your goals, due Friday at 11:59 PM.
terms.inRealLife: Honest answers help your trainer help you.
terms.emcNote: Due time and four objectives are from the live app.

terms.plain: The in-person gathering where your week is confirmed before the session.
terms.emcNote: [John to fill: what players actually do at muster]

terms.plain: The sign-up steps where you build your character and tell us about yourself.
terms.emcNote: [John to confirm what the papers cover]

terms.plain: A goal set for the whole Company or for a squad. Find them on the Missions board.
terms.emcNote: From the live app's Missions board.

terms.plain: A planned session of exercise. Check-in asks how many you got in this week.
terms.inRealLife: Any planned session counts. If you are new, start small.
terms.emcNote: [John to confirm what counts as a workout]

terms.plain: One group of repetitions.
terms.inRealLife: Example: 10 squats in a row is one set. Rest, then do another.

terms.plain: One full movement.
terms.inRealLife: One squat down and back up is one rep.

terms.plain: Steady work that raises your heart rate, like jogging, cycling or brisk walking.
Moving your joints through their full range so your body moves easily. Stretching is one kind.
Light movement before the main work to get your body ready.
Rate of Perceived Exertion. A 1 to 10 score for how hard something felt. 1 is very easy and 10 is all you have got.
terms.inRealLife: Use it to tell your trainer how a set felt.

terms.plain: Extra activities you can log beyond your regular workouts.

terms.plain: A standard gym exercise: lying on a bench and bending your elbows to lower a weight toward your forehead, then straightening your arms. It works the back of the arm.
